title: Live AWS integration tests can make pytest depend on external credentials and network state
reasoning: The AWS test class is skipped only when the application lacks an AWS Location API key or still uses the example place index. In any environment with real credentials, regular pytest collection will run live AWS Location calls against hard-coded cities. That makes the integration suite depend on network availability, AWS account configuration, service quota, place-index behavior, and billing-enabled external services, which can create flaky or unexpectedly slow CI/release runs.
recommendation: Gate these tests behind an explicit opt-in environment flag or pytest marker selection in addition to credential checks, and keep default test runs offline. Prefer mocking the AWS client for normal integration coverage and reserve live AWS calls for a separately named/manual smoke suite.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The file itself is the test suite behavior under review; it verifies AWS behavior only when enabled but does not protect the broader test command from accidentally running live network tests when credentials are present.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a collection/default-run check that AWS live tests are skipped unless the explicit opt-in flag is set, even when AWS settings contain real-looking values.
minimumFixScope: tests/integration/test_aws_location.py and the test settings or pytest marker configuration used by CI.
